Your voice is an instrument, and just like you could learn to play several chords on a guitar in no time, that wouldn't make you a guitarist any more than being able to sing a few songs without making your dogs howl along means you're a singer.

But, it doesn't take too long to learn to carry a tune, maybe a couple months of regular practice. Repeated, focused exercises several times a week will give you steady improvement. Hey a fellow opera singer on voat! At the 10 year mark how happy are you with your technique?

I had a very good coach for around 3 or 4 years and my voice got so much stronger during that period. I am currently on a long break from coaching and working hard at it for a number of reasons. I am contemplating starting up coaching again at some point. But I am still just a hobbyist at this point so I'm not sure how far I am going to go with it. Nothing beats the feeling, though, of being in the zone, having your voice all balanced up, and then being able to sail through some very dramatic material. My voice isn't in as good of shape as it was at its best and it is a real drag.

I've definitely made a lot of progress over the past 10 years. I'm very pleased with how much my technique freed my voice as a bass. I still have a long way to go, especially since my voice probably won't be fully mature for another 10 years, but it will all come with time.

Don't feel discouraged by being rusty. After reaching certain points with singing, even after extensive breaks, consistent practice will whip your voice back into shape much quicker than if you're just starting out. Muscle memory lasts a long time. That rush you're talking about is one of the greatest feelings I've ever experienced. It's truly zen.
